verdict_reason: The estimand is ||grad_h log P(y|h)||^2 at the observed next token, and the closed form the code uses for it - grad_h log P = W_y - E_p[W] - is exactly right: against float64 autograd through the real lm_head on gpt2 the maximum absolute difference is 1.27e-15 and the maximum relative difference 1.2e-8. There is no counterexample to the arithmetic. This GREEN is on the ESTIMATOR only; the shipped guard makes the task emit no value at all on a bf16 zoo, and the quantity is not invariant to the residual stream's arbitrary scale - both are recorded below under defects and comparable, per the axis separation.
comparable_reason: The value is not invariant under a function-preserving reparameterisation of the residual stream, so two models that compute the SAME function can report values differing by any factor. Verified exactly on pythia-70m (untied head): multiplying final_layer_norm.weight and .bias by c=2 and dividing embed_out.weight by 2 leaves the logits BIT-IDENTICAL (max |logit change| = 0.000e+00) while representation_sensitivity moves 0.385760 -> 0.096440, a ratio of exactly 0.250000 = 1/c^2. Across 7 models it is essentially a statistic of the unembedding matrix rather than of the function: pearson(representation_sensitivity, E_y||W_y - Wbar||^2) = +0.9726, spearman +0.9286. Any cross-model reading of this number is reading each model's arbitrary choice of residual-stream units. The scale-free repair is ||h||^2 * ||grad_h log P||^2, which is invariant to exactly this transformation.
normalized_variant: representation_sensitivity_scalefree (= mean over tokens of ||h||^2 * ||grad_h log P||^2), emitted by the task itself
github_reason: No code was ever released for this construction, and the cited source does not define it. Amari 1998, 'Natural Gradient Works Efficiently in Learning' (Neural Computation 10(2)), is a theory paper with no code, and it concerns the natural gradient / Fisher metric over PARAMETERS - its whole argument is that the EUCLIDEAN gradient norm is the coordinate-dependent object one should replace, which is precisely the object this task reports. The softmax score identity the code uses is elementary calculus, not an Amari result. I verified the identity myself against float64 autograd (above); that part is correct.
paper_reason: Amari 1998 publishes no value for this quantity and runs no language-model experiment, so there is nothing to reproduce. Note also the definitional slip the citation invites: E_{y ~ p}[||grad_h log p||^2] = tr(W^T (diag(p) - p p^T) W) IS the Fisher information of h, but the code evaluates the score at the OBSERVED next token, i.e. the empirical Fisher - a different object, and one that confounds sensitivity with per-token surprisal.
confounds_reason: Not a d_model proxy specifically, but a units artifact, which is worse. The 1/c^2 reparameterisation above is dispositive: an exactly logit-preserving change of variables moves the number by an arbitrary factor. Empirically it tracks a pure weight statistic at pearson +0.9726 over 7 models (E_y||W_y - Wbar||^2), and over the 8-model panel I ran it has spearman -0.913 with vocab_size and only -0.123 with d_model - i.e. what it is 'measuring' is how the unembedding rows are scaled and spread, which differs by tokenizer and initialisation rather than by anything about the representation.
defects: CODE, LIVE AND SEVERE: the linear-head guard threshold (information_geometry.py:102) is 1e-3, which is BELOW bfloat16's own eps of 7.81e-3, so it fires on every bf16 model and the task returns an error dict instead of a number. Verified on all 8 models I ran: every one errors under bf16. On gpt2 the measured guard value is rel = 0.0024515 (bf16), 0.0003066 (fp16, passes), 0.0 (fp32, passes). The study zoo runs bf16, and RERUN_LEDGER already records that this task 'produced no data at all'. The cause is dtype rounding, not a non-linear head.
CODE: the error message blames 'final logit softcapping' when the actual cause on every model I tested was dtype rounding. That message will send a future maintainer to the wrong architecture check.

CODE: _head_checked is set BEFORE validation (information_geometry.py:99), so a task instance that errors on its first call skips validation on every subsequent call and emits a number for a head it already rejected.

GAUGE: the reported quantity is not invariant to a function-preserving rescaling of the residual stream - measured ratio exactly 0.2500 = 1/c^2 at c=2 with bit-identical logits. This is a property of the estimand, not a bug in the code, but it makes cross-model values meaningless as reported.

ESTIMAND: the score is evaluated at the OBSERVED token, so the value is the empirical Fisher and is confounded with token surprisal, not the Fisher information the Amari citation implies. For a binary model at p = (0.9999, 0.0001) the same distribution yields ~1e-8 or ~0.9998 depending only on which label was observed, while tr(F_h) is unchanged.
CODE: per-document means are averaged with equal weight regardless of token count, so re-segmenting the same token stream changes the headline.
fix: 1) Set the guard tolerance from the model's own dtype (max(1e-3, 8 * torch.finfo(model.dtype).eps), i.e. ~6e-2 for bf16) or cast h and W to float32 before the check, and reword the message to 'recomputed logits differ beyond dtype tolerance' rather than naming softcapping. This alone restores the task on the entire bf16 zoo. 2) Set _head_checked only AFTER a successful check. 3) Emit a scale-invariant twin ||h||^2 * ||grad_h log P(y|h)||^2 (invariant to the c-rescaling I demonstrated) as the cross-model feature, keeping the raw value under its own name; or drop the raw value from the feature matrix. 4) If the Amari/Fisher framing is to be kept, emit tr(F_h) = sum_k p_k||W_k||^2 - ||sum_k p_k W_k||^2 as a label-free companion, and rename the current output true_token_score_norm. NORMALIZED-VARIANT AXIS (measured 2026-09-04): representation_sensitivity_scalefree is now emitted and I reproduced its invariance independently, by running the SHIPPED task on pythia-70m before and after scaling final_layer_norm.weight/.bias by c = 2 and dividing embed_out.weight by 2: the logits are bit-identical (max |delta| = 0.0), the raw value moves 0.4093387723 -> 0.1023346931 (exactly 1/c^2 = 0.25000000) and the scalefree value is unchanged at 79789.47461 (ratio 1.00000000). That closes the reparameterisation axis exactly, and it is the only twin in NORMALIZERS-adjacent code that does. It does NOT by itself make the column cross-model comparable, which is why this is YELLOW rather than GREEN: over 20 freshly run models the raw value's one significant architecture association is with vocabulary (rho = -0.691, p = 7e-04) and the scalefree twin reduces that to -0.144 (p = 0.5) while INTRODUCING a width term, rho(d_model) -0.191 -> -0.493 (p = 0.03) -- expected, since the ||h||^2 factor it multiplies in grows with width. Report it as the reparameterisation-invariant form, not as a size-free one.
